thread:
Sonya: heads-up — p99 latency jumped ~2x after yesterday's batching prefill/queue rollout. noticed around 17:40 UTC on a medium-sized pool. chart: https://graf.redwood/p/xyz (p99/5m)
Liam: saw that alert. runtime-bot shows the rollout completed at 17:34 UTC. @runtime-bot can you dump the rollout metadata?
runtime-bot: rollout completed: feature=batching-prefill-v2, change_id=chg_2024_11_18, targets=continuous-queue, started=17:30, finished=17:34
Sonya: thanks. initial hypothesis: prefill threshold lowered too aggressively, causing more small-shaped batches that pick the fallback kernel.
Deepak: FWIW my local microbench didn't show regression — but we didn't exercise the mixed short/long request blend we have in prod. could be a shape-triggered kernel flip.
Liam: I pulled a tiny slice of runtime logs (search for kernel decision lines). snippet:
```
2024-11-18T17:33:58Z INFO kernel-selector: selected kernel=matmul-optimized for batch_shape=[1,256]
2024-11-18T17:34:02Z INFO kernel-selector: selected kernel=generic-cuda for batch_shape=[3,32] reason=shape_mismatch
2024-11-18T17:34:04Z WARN kv-cache: evict_churn=0.42 hit_rate=0.71 -> 0.55 window=60s
2024-11-18T17:34:10Z INFO batcher: prefill_alloc=0.25 target_tokens=128 token_budget_used=0.88
```
Liam: note the kernel flip at 17:34:02 and kv hit-rate drop after the rollout — could be correlation.
Alex(SRE): p99 spike coincides with a small top-10 customer traffic burst (10% above baseline) — their requests are chatty short tokens which magnifies small-batch effects.
Sonya: if prefill is creating more heterogeneous batch shapes, the kernel-selector picks generic-cuda which is slower at our seq lengths. can we confirm which kernels are slower on these shapes? Liam, can you run the perf-profile command against a node we pulled logs from?
Liam: running: `./tools/profile_node --node-id=node-17 --shapes "[1x256,3x32]" --samples 200` will take ~3m. results:
```
shape [1,256] -> matmul-optimized avg_tok_ms=0.24
shape [3,32]  -> generic-cuda     avg_tok_ms=0.65
shape [2,64]  -> matmul-optimized avg_tok_ms=0.27
```
Liam: confirms generic-cuda is ~2.5x slower per-token for those small-wide shapes.
Deepak: that matches the throughput dip. Also kv-cache hit_rate drop suggests more new prefixes; prefill might be bypassing prefix caching if we allocate tokens differently.
Sonya: do we have metric that ties prefill allocations to kv cache eviction? maybe prefill is increasing prefix diversity because short requests are being combined with long ones.
Alex(SRE): here's the prod metric query I used: `sum by(pool) (kv_cache_evictions{env=prod} offset 5m)` — eviction delta spikes aligned with rollout window. I can share raw numbers if helpful.
Liam: quick replay test — I re-ran a traffic replay for the same minute with prefill=v1 (old) and prefill=v2 (rolled). v2 shows 28% higher p99 and 18% lower throughput.
Deepak: suggested mitigation: restore previous prefill threshold (v1) for continuous-queue on affected pools, and add a kernel affinity rule: prefer matmul-optimized for shapes with seq>=64 and batch_size<=2. also throttle prefill for pools with >20% short-request traffic.
Sonya: +1 to revert as hotfix. Postmortem follow-ups: (1) add unit test that replays mixed short/long shapes during rollout checks, (2) add a trace tag that records kernel-reason on p99 traces, (3) tune token_budget target to avoid aggressive prefix mixing.
Liam: I'll prepare the revert PR now. assigning myself. PR will set prefill-v2->disabled for continuous-queue and include a canary flag for gradual enabling. ETA 30m.
runtime-bot: deploy triggered: revert/prefill-v2 -> canary=false, targets=continuous-queue, change_id=chg_2024_11_18-revert, started=17:52
Sonya: after revert, keep monitoring kv hit-rate and kernel-selection logs. Alex — can you watch p99 for the next 30m and post updates?
Alex(SRE): yup monitoring. initial post-revert snapshot: p99 back down ~15% vs peak, kv_hit_rate recovering to 0.68 in the last 3m. will update if it doesn't settle.
Sonya: thanks team. we'll follow up with an RCA doc once we have full traces. small action items in the thread: @Liam PR, @Deepak kernel-affinity proposal, @Alex keep watching. :eyes:
